newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian bourse volume bolstered by bloc sales.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian bourse volume bolstered by bloc sales.

text.p: Jordan's stock exchange posted a new five-month low at end of weekly trade on Wednesday but two bloc sales bolstered volume substantially, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell 0.16 percent to 150.22 points, its lowest level since November, in turnover of 858,189 dinars ($1,212,134) dominated by bloc sales.
The market has seen falls this week triggered by shares going ex-dividend which dealers expect to continue to put downward pressure on price levels for the coming few weeks.
Two bloc sales in International Tobacco, which announced stronger than expected 1996 profits, and Arab International Hotel alone accounted for nearly half the day's volume.
AIHO was unchanged at 4.35 dinars in 175,171 dinars worth of trade in activity which was otherwise focused on some banks and industrials.
Jordan Investment Finance Bank rose 4.92 percent to 3.41 dinars and Jordan Cement Factory rose 1.92 percent to 3.72 dinars in 37,267 dinars worth of trade.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 19 to eight, with another four trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.03 points to 79.97 points, 4.10 percent down from the start of the year.
